title: Jeremiah Chapter 9 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 9 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 9 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 9.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 9, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Oh that my head were waters, and mine eyes a fountain of tears
Take ye heed every one of his neighbour
Therefore thus saith the LORD of hosts
Their tongue is as an arrow shot out
questions.correctAnswer: Oh that my head were waters, and mine eyes a fountain of tears
questions.explanation: This phrase appears first in Jeremiah 9:1, expressing the prophet's deep sorrow.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah wish for in Jeremiah 9:2?
options: A lodging place of wayfaring men
questions.correctAnswer: A lodging place of wayfaring men
questions.explanation: Jeremiah expresses a desire for a lodging place in the wilderness in Jeremiah 9:2.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 9:3, what do the people bend their tongues like?
questions.correctAnswer: A bow for lies
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:3 states that they bend their tongues like their bow for lies.

questions.question: What should every one take heed of according to Jeremiah 9:4?
questions.correctAnswer: His neighbor
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:4 instructs to take heed of every one of his neighbor.

questions.question: What have the people taught their tongues to do in Jeremiah 9:5?
questions.correctAnswer: Speak lies
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:5 mentions that they have taught their tongue to speak lies.

questions.question: What is said about the habitation in Jeremiah 9:6?
options: It is a place of peace
It is in the midst of deceit
It is blessed by the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: It is in the midst of deceit
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:6 states that their habitation is in the midst of deceit.

questions.question: What does the LORD say He will do in Jeremiah 9:7?
questions.correctAnswer: Melt them and try them
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:7 conveys that the LORD will melt them and try them.

questions.question: What is the nature of their tongue in Jeremiah 9:8?
options: It is a source of wisdom
It is as an arrow shot out
It is a tool for healing
questions.correctAnswer: It is as an arrow shot out
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:8 describes their tongue as an arrow shot out that speaketh deceit.

questions.question: What does the LORD say He will do in Jeremiah 9:9?
questions.correctAnswer: Visit them for these things
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:9 asks if the LORD will not visit them for these things.

questions.question: The people are described as an assembly of what in Jeremiah 9:2?
questions.correctAnswer: Treacherous men
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:2 refers to them as an assembly of treacherous men.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 9:3, how do the people proceed?
questions.correctAnswer: From evil to evil
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:3 states that they proceed from evil to evil.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah wishes to weep day and night for the slain of his people.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: This is directly stated in Jeremiah 9:1 where he expresses his sorrow.

questions.question: True or False: The people are described as faithful and trustworthy.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The text indicates their treachery and deceit, implying they are not trustworthy.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD will bless the people for their truthfulness.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The LORD speaks of judgment rather than blessing due to their deceit and lies.

questions.question: True or False: The people in Jeremiah 9 are described as wise and just.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The chapter describes them as adulterers and treacherous, lacking wisdom and justice.

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 9 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 9 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 9:10, what will happen to the mountains and wilderness?
options: The mountains will take up a weeping and wailing, and the wilderness will be burned up
The mountains will be covered with trees, and the wilderness will flourish
The mountains will be silent, and the wilderness will be filled with animals
The mountains will shine brightly, and the wilderness will be peaceful
questions.correctAnswer: The mountains will take up a weeping and wailing, and the wilderness will be burned up
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:10 states, 'For the mountains will I take up a weeping and wailing, and for the habitations of the wilderness a lamentation, because they are burned up...'

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 9:15 promise will happen if the people walk after the imagination of their own heart and Baalim as described in Jeremiah 9:14?
options: The LORD will feed them with wormwood and give them water of gall to drink
The LORD will bless them with abundant harvests
The LORD will protect them from their enemies
The LORD will restore their cities and homes
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will feed them with wormwood and give them water of gall to drink
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:15 says, 'Therefore thus saith the LORD of hosts... I will feed them, even this people, with wormwood, and give them water of gall to drink,' which is a consequence of their actions in 9:14.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 9:11 say will happen to Jerusalem and the cities of Judah?
options: They will become heaps and desolate, without inhabitants
They will be rebuilt and full of people
They will be surrounded by armies but remain strong
They will be places of great peace and prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: They will become heaps and desolate, without inhabitants
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:11 states, 'And I will make Jerusalem heaps, and a den of dragons; and I will make the cities of Judah desolate, without an inhabitant.'

questions.question: How do Jeremiah 9:12 and 9:13 connect in explaining the cause of the land perishing?
options: Jeremiah 9:12 asks who can understand the disaster, and 9:13 answers because they forsook the LORD's law
Jeremiah 9:12 predicts a harvest, and 9:13 describes the planting season
Jeremiah 9:12 describes a battle, and 9:13 tells of the victory
Jeremiah 9:12 calls for celebration, and 9:13 explains the reason for joy
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah 9:12 asks who can understand the disaster, and 9:13 answers because they forsook the LORD's law
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:12 questions who can understand why the land perishes, and 9:13 explains it is because they have forsaken the LORD's law.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 9:16, what will the LORD do to the people because they have forsaken His law?
options: Scatter them among heathen nations and send a sword after them
Bless them with peace and prosperity
Gather them back to their land
questions.correctAnswer: Scatter them among heathen nations and send a sword after them
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:16 says, 'I will scatter them also among the heathen... and I will send a sword after them, till I have consumed them,' as a punishment for forsaking God's law.

questions.question: What is the purpose of calling for the mourning women and cunning women in Jeremiah 9:17-18?
options: To make haste and take up a wailing so that eyes may run down with tears
To prepare a feast for the people
To teach the people about wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: To make haste and take up a wailing so that eyes may run down with tears
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:17-18 commands to call mourning and cunning women to wail so that eyes may run down with tears, indicating deep lamentation.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah express a desire for in Jeremiah 9:1 that reflects his emotional state regarding the people?
options: That his head were waters and his eyes a fountain of tears to weep for the slain
That he might rejoice and sing praises
That he might forget the troubles of the people
That he might travel to other lands
questions.correctAnswer: That his head were waters and his eyes a fountain of tears to weep for the slain
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:1 states, 'Oh that my head were waters, and mine eyes a fountain of tears, that I might weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people!' indicating deep sorrow.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 9:6, what is the nature of the people's habitation and its effect on their knowledge of God?
options: Their habitation is in deceit, and through deceit they refuse to know God
Their habitation is peaceful, and they know God well
Their habitation is prosperous, and they honor God
Their habitation is isolated, and they seek God earnestly
questions.correctAnswer: Their habitation is in deceit, and through deceit they refuse to know God
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:6 says, 'Thine habitation is in the midst of deceit; through deceit they refuse to know me,' describing the people's spiritual condition.

questions.question: What warning does Jeremiah 9:9 give regarding the LORD's response to deceitful and treacherous behavior?
options: The LORD will visit them and his soul will be avenged on such a nation
The LORD will ignore their sins
The LORD will reward them for their peace
The LORD will bless their prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will visit them and his soul will be avenged on such a nation
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:9 states, 'Shall I not visit them for these things? saith the LORD: shall not my soul be avenged on such a nation as this?' showing divine judgment is certain.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah describe the people's speech in Jeremiah 9:3?
options: They bend their tongues like bows for lies and proceed from evil to evil
questions.correctAnswer: They bend their tongues like bows for lies and proceed from evil to evil
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:3 says, 'And they bend their tongues like their bow for lies... for they proceed from evil to evil,' describing their deceitful nature.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 9:4 warn about trusting neighbors and brothers?
options: Do not trust any brother or neighbor because they will supplant and slander
Trust fully in brothers and neighbors
Ignore neighbors and focus on strangers
questions.correctAnswer: Do not trust any brother or neighbor because they will supplant and slander
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:4 instructs, 'Take ye heed every one of his neighbour, and trust ye not in any brother: for every brother will utterly supplant, and every neighbour will walk with slanders.'

questions.question: What reason does Jeremiah give in 9:13-14 for the land perishing and being burned up?
options: Because they forsook God's law and walked after their own heart and Baalim
questions.correctAnswer: Because they forsook God's law and walked after their own heart and Baalim
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:13-14 explains the land perishes because 'they have forsaken my law... and have walked after the imagination of their own heart, and after Baalim...'

questions.question: What is the effect of deceitful speech as described in Jeremiah 9:8?
options: One speaks peaceably with the mouth but hides an ambush in the heart
One always speaks truth and peace
One remains silent to avoid conflict
questions.correctAnswer: One speaks peaceably with the mouth but hides an ambush in the heart
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:8 says, 'one speaketh peaceably to his neighbour with his mouth, but in heart he layeth his wait,' showing duplicity in speech.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 9:2 expresses a wish to leave the people because they are adulterers and treacherous.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:2 states, 'Oh that I had in the wilderness a lodging place of wayfaring men; that I might leave my people... for they be all adulterers, an assembly of treacherous men.'

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 9:10 says that the voice of the cattle will be heard in the burned wilderness.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:10 states that none can hear the voice of the cattle because the wilderness is burned up, indicating silence, not sound.

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 9 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 9.

questions.question: What is heard out of Zion according to Jeremiah 9:19?
questions.correctAnswer: A voice of wailing
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:19 states, 'For a voice of wailing is heard out of Zion...' indicating lamentation and sorrow.

questions.question: Who does the Lord instruct to hear His word in Jeremiah 9:20?
questions.correctAnswer: Women
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:20 says, 'Yet hear the word of the LORD, O ye women...' highlighting their role in the lament.

questions.question: What has entered into the palaces according to Jeremiah 9:21?
questions.correctAnswer: Death
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:21 states, 'For death is come up into our windows, and is entered into our palaces...' indicating imminent judgment.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 9:22, how shall the carcasses of men fall?
options: As dung upon the open field
questions.correctAnswer: As dung upon the open field
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:22 says, 'Even the carcases of men shall fall as dung upon the open field...' stressing the dire consequences of sin.

questions.question: What should the wise man not glory in, according to Jeremiah 9:23?
questions.correctAnswer: His wisdom
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:23 states, 'Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom...' emphasizing the futility of pride in human achievements.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 9:24, what does the Lord delight in?
questions.correctAnswer: Understanding and knowing Him
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:24 says, 'for in these things I delight, saith the LORD...' highlighting the value of relationship with God.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'wailing' in Jeremiah 9:20 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Lamentation
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term for 'wailing' conveys a deep expression of grief and sorrow, fitting the context of Jeremiah's lament.

questions.question: What literary device is predominantly used in Jeremiah 9:23-24?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:23-24 utilizes parallelism by contrasting what should not be glorified with what should be valued.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of lamentation in Jeremiah 9:19?
questions.correctAnswer: Lamentations 1:1
questions.explanation: Lamentations 1:1 expresses sorrow over Jerusalem, similar to the wailing in Jeremiah 9:19.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the judgment mentioned in Jeremiah 9:25?
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 2:6
questions.explanation: Romans 2:6 aligns with the theme of judgment and accountability seen in Jeremiah 9:25.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Jeremiah 9:19?
options: A description of the land's desolation
questions.correctAnswer: A lament over the people
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:18 precedes 9:19, continuing the theme of mourning for the people's plight.

questions.question: What does the term 'circumcised' refer to in the context of Jeremiah 9:25?
questions.correctAnswer: Covenantal identity
questions.explanation: The term 'circumcised' in Jeremiah 9:25 signifies the identity of God's covenant people, emphasizing the need for true faith.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 9:26 reveal about the nations mentioned?
questions.correctAnswer: They are uncircumcised
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:26 emphasizes that all the nations mentioned are uncircumcised, indicating their separation from God's covenant.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah laments for the slain of his people in Jeremiah 9:1.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:1 reveals his deep sorrow, expressing a desire to weep for the slain of his people.

questions.question: True or False: The wise man is encouraged to glory in his wisdom according to Jeremiah 9:23.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:23 explicitly states that the wise man should not glory in his wisdom, which is contrary to the statement.

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 9 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 9 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Jeremiah 9:1 teach about human sin?
options: Human sin causes deep communal grief and divine sorrow
Human sin is easily forgiven without repentance
Human sin is primarily a failure of knowledge
Human sin has no impact on God's people
questions.correctAnswer: Human sin causes deep communal grief and divine sorrow
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:1 expresses the prophet's desire to weep day and night for the slain of his people, indicating the profound grief caused by their sin and its consequences.

questions.question: What doctrine does Jeremiah 9:3 teach about God's knowledge of human wickedness?
options: God fully knows the progression of evil from one sin to another
God is unaware of the evil intentions of mankind
Human wickedness can hide from God's sight
God only judges external actions, not internal motives
questions.correctAnswer: God fully knows the progression of evil from one sin to another
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:3 states that they proceed from evil to evil and know not God, indicating God's full awareness of their continual wickedness.

questions.question: What doctrine does Jeremiah 9:23-24 teach about true wisdom and glory?
options: True glory is found in understanding and knowing God, who exercises lovingkindness, judgment, and righteousness
True wisdom is in human strength and riches
Glory is to be found in intellectual achievements
Human pride in power is the highest spiritual attainment
questions.correctAnswer: True glory is found in understanding and knowing God, who exercises lovingkindness, judgment, and righteousness
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:23-24 explicitly contrasts human wisdom, might, and riches with the glory that comes from knowing God and His character.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Jeremiah 9:7 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:7 declares that the LORD will melt and try His people, showing His sovereign authority over judgment and refinement.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Jeremiah 9:9 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Justice
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:9 shows God’s righteous judgment as He declares His soul will be avenged upon the nation for their sins.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 9:10 connect to the broader biblical theme of divine judgment?
options: It foreshadows the desolation of creation due to human sin, akin to the wilderness imagery in Isaiah
It teaches that animals are indifferent to human sin
It affirms that environmental destruction is unrelated to divine judgment
It predicts a new Eden without wilderness
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the desolation of creation due to human sin, akin to the wilderness imagery in Isaiah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:10’s lament over desolation parallels other prophetic judgments like Isaiah’s wilderness imagery, indicating the cosmic extent of judgment.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 9:15-16 prepare the redemptive-historical theme of exile and restoration?
options: By announcing God’s punishment through bitterness and scattering among nations, setting the stage for future restoration
By promising immediate restoration without consequences
By denying any consequences for disobedience
By focusing solely on personal repentance without national consequences
questions.correctAnswer: By announcing God’s punishment through bitterness and scattering among nations, setting the stage for future restoration
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:15-16 speaks of feeding the people wormwood and scattering them, which anticipates the exile and eventual restoration narrative.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Jeremiah 9:4 and Jeremiah 9:5 teach about human sinfulness?
options: Human sinfulness corrupts relationships, breeding distrust, deceit, and moral weariness
Human sinfulness is only an individual issue, not social
Sin only affects public worship, not personal relationships
Human sinfulness can be overcome without divine intervention
questions.correctAnswer: Human sinfulness corrupts relationships, breeding distrust, deceit, and moral weariness
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:4-5 describes neighbors and brothers betraying and deceiving each other, emphasizing sin’s impact on community and trust.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 9:12 and Jeremiah 9:13 teach about the consequences of forsaking God’s law?
options: Forsaking God’s law results in the land perishing and becoming desolate
Forsaking God’s law leads to immediate prosperity
The land’s condition is unrelated to obedience to God’s law
Forsaking God’s law only affects individual spirituality
questions.correctAnswer: Forsaking God’s law results in the land perishing and becoming desolate
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:12-13 links the land’s desolation directly to the people’s abandonment of God’s law and disobedience.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 9:17 and Jeremiah 9:20 teach about the role of public lamentation?
options: Public lamentation is a communal response to judgment that involves teaching future generations
Lamentation should be hidden and private only
Lamentation is unnecessary in the face of divine judgment
Lamentation is a sign of despair without hope
questions.correctAnswer: Public lamentation is a communal response to judgment that involves teaching future generations
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:17 and 9:20 call for mourning women and teaching daughters lamentation, showing lament as a communal and instructive practice.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Jeremiah 9:10-11 depicts an overly harsh and unjust God who destroys all creation. What does the passage actually teach?
options: God’s judgment is just and results in desolation due to human sinfulness, not arbitrary destruction
God destroys creation without cause or justice
God’s wrath is indiscriminate and unrestrained
The passage promotes a nihilistic worldview denying God’s justice
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment is just and results in desolation due to human sinfulness, not arbitrary destruction
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:10-11 describes desolation as a consequence of Israel’s sin, emphasizing divine justice rather than arbitrary wrath.

questions.question: What doctrine does Jeremiah 9:6 teach about the human refusal to know God?
options: Deceit leads to spiritual blindness and rejection of God's knowledge
Humans can know God regardless of moral condition
God hides Himself from those who sin
Knowledge of God is irrelevant to salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Deceit leads to spiritual blindness and rejection of God's knowledge
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:6 states that through deceit they refuse to know God, showing that sin corrupts true knowledge of God.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Jeremiah 9:24 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Lovingkindness
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:24 states God exercises lovingkindness, judgment, and righteousness, highlighting His lovingkindness as a key attribute.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 9:25-26 teach about the nature of covenant membership?
options: True covenant membership is circumcision of the heart, not just physical circumcision
Physical circumcision guarantees salvation regardless of the heart
Covenant membership is based on ethnicity alone
questions.correctAnswer: True covenant membership is circumcision of the heart, not just physical circumcision
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:25-26 contrasts physical circumcision with the uncircumcised heart, teaching the necessity of inner spiritual transformation.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 9:8 prepare for New Testament teachings on hypocrisy and deceit?
options: It anticipates Jesus’ condemnation of hypocritical speech and deceitful hearts
It endorses deceptive speech as a survival tactic
It ignores the problem of hypocrisy in faith communities
It limits deceit to Israel without broader application
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates Jesus’ condemnation of hypocritical speech and deceitful hearts
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 9:8’s depiction of deceitful tongues aligns with Jesus’ later denunciations of hypocrisy in Matthew 23.
